hookLine: He spent thirty years on death row for murders he didn't commit

cards.title: A Manager Shot Dead
cards.subtitle: Two restaurant robberies turned fatal in Birmingham

cards.title: The Wrong Gun
cards.subtitle: Police matched bullets to a revolver from his mother's house

cards.title: Expert for Hire
cards.subtitle: His court-appointed attorney could barely afford a forensics expert

cards.title: Freedom at Fifty-Eight
cards.subtitle: Advanced ballistics testing proved the gun was never fired

ctaLine: Follow Cold Trail for cases the mainstream forgot
voiceover:
Anthony Ray Hinton walked out of Alabama's death row in twenty fifteen after three decades in a five by seven cell.

He was twenty nine when police arrested him for two restaurant murders in Birmingham. He had alibis placing him fifteen miles away at work.

Prosecutors built their case on a single piece of evidence: bullets that an expert claimed matched a revolver found at his mother's home.

His defense attorney had a thousand dollar budget for experts. The state's ballistics witness went unchallenged, despite a history of questionable testimony.

New testing proved the gun never fired those bullets. Hinton was fifty eight when he finally walked free.
